question: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Himalayas**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas are the physical feature that prevents cold winds from Central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinent**
 
• The **Himalayas are a lofty mountain range that blocks cold winds from Central Asia from entering India.**
 
• The Himalayas' height, location, and complex topography significantly impact the climate of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **Himalayas also influence the monsoons, forcing the rain-bearing winds to lose most of their moisture before crossing the range. **
 
• The Himalayas cause the Indian subcontinent to experience milder winters than Central Asia.
 
• **Northern India also has higher temperatures than other areas on the same latitudes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian plain**s

 
 
• **The Northern Plains, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain**, are the granaries of India and the foundation for early civilizations.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the **rivers Ganga**, **Yamuna**, **Brahmaputra**, and their tributaries.
 
• It stretches across northern and northeastern India, covering states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **West Bengal**, **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The Indo-Gangetic plain is characterized by fertile soils, making it one of the most important agricultural regions in India.
 
• It is densely populated, with major cities like **Delhi**, **Kolkata**, **Lucknow**, and **Patna** located along its course.
 
 
 
• **Indian desert**
 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is India's largest desert, covering about 77,000 square miles.
 
• The Thar Desert spans across parts of **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, **Punjab**, and **Haryana** in India, extending into **Pakistan**.
 
• It covers around **200,000 square kilometres** in India, primarily in the state of Rajasthan.
 
• The desert supports sparse vegetation like **cactus**, **acacia trees**, and **scrub plants**.
 
 
 
• **Coastal area**s
 
 
• **India's coastal areas include the coastal states of Gujarat**, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal, as well as the coastal union territories of Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Lakshadweep Islands, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Coastal plains are low-lying**, flat areas of land that are adjacent to the sea or ocean.
 
• The elevation of the land increases gradually from the sea to the highlands. 
 
• **India's other main physical features include the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.**
